report.summary: 四张运行截图里整体轮廓已像现代主战坦克，但只有首上倾角（K5）能从画面确认；K1~K4 因缺标尺、正交视图与可辨的炮塔俯视轮廓而无法证实。侧裙骨架化、炮管竹节感、车体底前缘外伸平板是最明显的玩具感部位。

findings.text: 侧裙缺失：I0/I1 中负重轮上方只有细横杆加竖向支撑的骨架，整个行走机构裸露，是最强的玩具感来源
炮管由多节同心圆柱叠成、节间有明显台阶，像竹节/伸缩管；I0、I3 中炮口端是异常粗大的空心管口
I1 侧视中炮口到车体前缘约占车体长 0.37，反推含炮管全长≈11m，与契约 10.0 对不上（也可能是透视夸大），需核对程序内实际米制值
I0、I3 中车体底前缘有一块水平外伸平板，像托板/底板，与首上装甲下缘不贴合
I2 俯视里炮塔与车体被迷彩连成一片、车尾还被裁掉，炮塔俯视楔形无法判读；I1 侧视炮塔接近方正长方体、前脸近乎垂直
I0/I1 中托带轮不可见，负重轮顶与车体底之间是空档，缺少悬挂摆臂、托带轮等中间件

本轮理解：用 three.js 做一个单文件 HTML：极其精细的现代主战坦克，可预览、可操控，写实帅气、炫技写真；不读取文件夹内其他文件。

正向补充与建议
- 依赖与打包前提：用 importmap 锁定版本（如 three@0.160.0），映射 three 到 build/three.module.js、three/addons/ 到 examples/jsm/，再引 RoomEnvironment 与 OrbitControls（环绕控制也可自写以少一个请求）。注意 file:// 下用相对路径加载 addons 会 CORS 失败，必须走 https CDN；好处是零外部贴图/模型文件，全部程序化生成，天然满足单文件。
- 比例基准先行：以米为单位（1 单位 = 1 米），车体长 7.6~8.0、全宽 3.6~3.8、炮塔顶 2.4~2.7、含炮管全长 9.8~10.0，负重轮 7 对（豹2/M1 系）或 6 对（T 系）。比例不准是最容易翻车的点——炮塔偏高、履带偏窄、负重轮偏少会立刻变玩具；相机默认距离 12~16 m、fov 35~45（长焦压缩才有写真感，默认 fov 50+ 广角会让坦克显小且透视失真）。
- 倒角几何是精细感的最大单点收益：装甲面用 ExtrudeGeometry 沿 Z 挤出 2D 轮廓并开 bevel（bevelThickness/bevelSize 约 0.015~0.03、bevelSegments 2），倒角边才能吃到环境高光；纯 BoxGeometry + 平色会像塑料。前提与反例：bevelSize 必须小于轮廓最短边，非凸轮廓（带缺口的炮塔楔形）会自交破面，需拆成 2~3 个凸件拼接；小零件别过度倒角，否则像肥皂。
- 履带用等弧长重采样的闭合路径 + InstancedMesh：路径 = 底部直线段 + 前后圆弧段 + 顶部直线段，按弧长把整圈重采样成 N 节（节距取 0.17~0.19 m，节数由周长决定），每节取切向生成矩阵；滚动只需把弧长偏移量按行进距离累加。两个常见 bug：按段各自均分会造成拐角处节距不均、视觉上打滑；路径不沿外法线偏移半个链板厚度会穿模进负重轮。80 节/侧 ×2 = 1 个 draw call，是细节/性能比最高的零件。
- 材质全部 CanvasTexture 程序化，不依赖任何外部文件：512² 值噪声做 roughnessMap（装甲 0.35~0.55、轮胎/胶裙 0.85、玻璃 0.05）；细长随机线叠加划痕雨痕；2048² 贝塞尔斑块画 NATO 三色迷彩当 map（不贴迷彩即使几何再精细也像未涂装样车）。设 anisotropy = renderer.capabilities.getMaxAnisotropy()，按每米 0.5~1 次 repeat 避免拉伸；金属度别给满，装甲 metalness 0.2~0.4 比 1.0 更真实。
- 光照是写实 vs 塑料的杠杆点：用 PMREMGenerator.fromScene(new RoomEnvironment(), 0.04) 得到 scene.environment，零外部 HDR 就有 IBL 反射；再叠一盏 45° 侧逆光 DirectionalLight（intensity 2~3）投 2048 阴影，shadow.normalBias 约 0.02、bias 约 -0.0005 消除平板上的阴影痤疮；渲染器 ACESFilmicToneMapping + exposure 1.0~1.3。这比堆后处理更划算。
- 动作分组决定像不像真车：炮管后坐只动炮管 + 炮盾，炮塔不参与——临界阻尼弹簧，后坐 0.25~0.35 m / 70~90 ms，复进 300~400 ms 带回弹过冲，同时车体几毫米俯仰反冲。炮塔用指针锁定模式随鼠标，但加 20~30°/s 转向上限与惯性减速，火炮俯仰 -9°~+20°。开火加炮口 additive 平面 + PointLight（60~80 ms 衰减）+ 贴地扩散尘环，观感提升大且几乎不耗性能。

Fix these plus the metalness of barrel/running gear/periscope glass, then verify three numbers headlessly instead of pixels.
assumptions: three r160 EffectComposer caches the renderer pixel ratio at construction and multiplies it in setSize(); UnrealBloomPass.setSize and GTAOPass.setSize take drawing-buffer pixels, so passing CSS pixels undersizes them on dpr>1. (High confidence, standard r160 source behaviour, but not verified against the actual CDN file in this environment.)

The model's +Z end is the rear, inferred from sprocket-rear/idler-front (F0), the deck slope, and the exhaust emitter at lz=+3.6 (E411); the muzzle/drive-direction assertions in the contribution are there so this is checked, not trusted.

findings.text: Post passes are re-sized in CSS pixels after the composer already sized them in drawing-buffer pixels: onResize (2366-2375) calls composer.setSize(w,h) then bloom.setSize(w,h) and ao.setSize(w,h); savePNG (2351-2364) raises the pixel ratio to as much as 3 without updating the composer's cached ratio. Consequence on any dpr=2 display: bloom mips and GTAO depth/normal targets run at half resolution (blocky glow, halo-y AO around the tracks), and the "high-res" export is an upscale of a lower-res post chain.

BokehPass defaults were changed from aperture 0.00035 / maxblur 0.009 (E399, line 2124) to aperture 0.03 / maxblur 0.012 (read, line 2124), and the per-frame driver sets 0.006-0.061 (read, line 2338). Since CoC = clamp((depth-focus)*aperture, +-maxblur) in UV units, the blur saturates 0.2-2 m from the focus plane - i.e. photo mode, the mode meant for the showcase PNG, is at maximum blur over almost the whole frame.

Two independent fog/lighting definitions exist in the file: buildEnvironment (fog 0xb9b3a0, sun 3.5, fill 0.42, hemi 0.42, at 972-987) and boot (fog 0xb9b3a0 again, SUN 2.8, hemi 0.45, at 2413-2423). Separately, SUNOFF is initialised to (0,0,0) (2377) while the loop positions the sun at TANK.pos + SUNOFF with the target on the tank (E411, 2311-2315), so any path where SUNOFF is not assigned gives light position == target: degenerate direction and shadow matrix, i.e. a black/garbage first frame rather than a merely ugly one.

Running gear and gun tube are set up as shiny metal with only a 1024x512 procedural sky as environment: MAT.steel metalness 0.92 / roughness 0.55, MAT.track 0.88 / 0.6, MAT.gunSteel 0.9 / 0.44 / envMapIntensity 1.2 (lines 735-739), and MAT.glass is a MeshPhysicalMaterial with metalness 0.55 (line 740). The gun tube is the largest specular object in the hero frame and will read as a chrome streak; the periscope blocks read as black mirrors.

Vehicle orientation vs boot camera: idlerZ = -3.36 / sprkZ = +3.36 (real M1 drives from rear sprockets), the hull deck is flat toward +Z and slopes down over the last ~2 m toward -Z, and engine haze is emitted at lz = +3.6 (E411, 2302-2307) - so the rear is +Z, while CAM.position is (8.4, 3.6, 10.5) (read, 2401) looking at the origin: the first frame is a rear 3/4 with the gun pointing away, at d=13.6 m / 38.7 deg off-axis, filling only ~27% of frame width at fov 46.

Threshold and emissive intensity must be moved together.

The sun is repositioned every frame to follow the tank (E411, 2311-2315) with no texel snapping, so ground shadow edges crawl and shimmer continuously while driving; the shadow ortho box is fixed at +-19 m at 2048 (read, 976-981), i.e. 18.6 mm/texel, when +-13 m (12.7 mm/texel) already contains a 9.8 m vehicle plus its shadow projection.

MAT.sand (0x9d8f76 with albedo + normal + roughness maps) and MAT.sandFar (0x9a8c74, no maps) coexist (lines 750-751) and FogExp2 0xb9b3a0 is hardcoded twice (972 and 2413) while the sky's horizon colour lives inside texSky: the first frame can show a texture-detail ring where the near terrain ends and a hard horizon seam if the sky's horizon band is not exactly 0xb9b3a0.

Current intent: Deliver a single self-contained HTML file that uses three.js to render an extremely detailed modern main battle tank, viewable in an orbit-style preview and drivable/controllable, with realism and showcase-grade ('photo-like', show-off) visual quality; do not open or preview any other file in the folder.

Clarification
- "Do not preview any other files in the folder" is read as: the only output is the one .html file — do not read, list, or display any other file in the folder, and the HTML must not fetch external assets (textures, models, HDRs) from that folder.
- "Can preview and control" is read as both modes in the same page: free orbit inspection with close-up zoom, plus live driving and turret/gun control.
- "Show-off photo" is read as showcase-quality rendering (PBR materials, tuned lighting, post-processing) plus optionally a photo/screenshot mode — not as a literal portrait image request.

Positive additions and suggestions
- Structure the deliverable as one HTML file using an ES-module importmap pinned to a specific three.js version, pulling OrbitControls, EffectComposer and RoomEnvironment from 'three/addons/'. All geometry, textures and environment must be generated in code (CanvasTexture, PMREMGenerator) because the single-file + no-other-files constraint rules out external assets; if the CDN is unreachable, degrade to flat lit materials rather than crashing.
- Build the tank from a parametric blueprint instead of loose primitives: hull as THREE.Shape profile (glacis, sponsons, engine deck) extruded with bevel for hard edges, turret as faceted wedge plates stacked with small offsets, and a named group hierarchy (hull / turret / barrel / roadWheel[i] / track[i]) so animation and later edits stay tractable.
- Use real-world metres so camera FOV, shadow bias and speed values are physically sensible: ~7.6 m hull, ~9.8 m overall with gun, 3.7 m width, 2.4 m height, 6–7 road wheels per side, ~6.6 m gun. Inconsistent scale is the most common reason such models read as toys.
- Spend the detail budget on things that survive close orbit inspection: hatch hinges and handles, periscope blocks with dark glass, sight windows, weld beads as TubeGeometry along seams, bolt rows and ERA blocks as InstancedMesh, tow cables/hooks, mesh stowage baskets, 2x6 smoke-grenade banks, thermal-sleeve segments plus bore evacuator on the barrel, spare track links on the turret.
- Tracks are the highest-ROI element: define one closed CatmullRomCurve3 around sprocket, idler, road wheels and return rollers, place link instances via InstancedMesh from curve.getPointAt/getTangentAt, and animate by advancing a scalar offset at (wheel angular velocity x radius) in both directions — so track speed matches ground speed instead of a fake texture scroll.
- For material realism use separate sets and generate their maps in-canvas: painted armour (roughness 0.6–0.75, metalness ~0.15) with procedural cast-steel mottling and edge chipping, bare steel tracks (metalness ~0.9, roughness ~0.45), rubber rims, and optical glass (roughness ~0.05, high envMapIntensity). RoomEnvironment + PMREM gives PBR reflections with no HDR file.
- Lighting/tone mapping decides whether it looks photographed: ACESFilmicToneMapping + SRGBColorSpace, one shadow-casting directional 'sun' with the shadow camera fitted tightly to the tank bounds, normalBias ~0.02 and bias ~-0.0005 to kill acne on flat armour plates, plus hemisphere fill and a subtle ground contact darkening.
- Post-processing is where 'showing off' is actually earned: EffectComposer chain of SSAO/GTAO -> bloom (threshold ~0.9 to avoid blowing out sunlit hull) -> SMAA, and a photo mode (P) with cinematic camera, BokehPass depth of field, vignette/grain and canvas screenshot download.
- Controls and feel: WASD torque-based drive with brake, independent 360-degree turret traverse and gun elevation clamped to roughly -9 to +20 degrees, mouse-look aiming, and firing that recoils the barrel ~0.3 m over ~60 ms with a damped hull rock, muzzle flash plus point-light flare, and a dust puff decal-free at the raycast impact point. Independent turret motion is what separates 'tank' from 'car with a gun'.
- Suspension: raycast each road wheel to a ground heightfield and offset wheels with damped springs, add slight hull pitch under acceleration/braking and a small speed-linked vibration for engine feel — cheap, and it removes the 'floating box' look while driving.
- Cameras and HUD: damped OrbitControls with polar limits so the ground is never seen from below, spring-follow chase camera, gunner's sight with an SVG NATO reticle and stepped 3x/10x zoom, commander panorama, and HUD readouts for speed, RPM/gear, turret azimuth, gun elevation, ammo state, FPS.
- Performance guardrails: InstancedMesh for tracks/bolts/ERA, shared geometries and materials, zero per-frame allocations (reuse scratch Vector3/Quaternion), pixelRatio capped at 2, and an auto-quality toggle that drops SSAO/DOF when frame time exceeds ~20 ms.
- Known failure modes to design against: z-fighting between layered armour plates (0.5–1 mm offsets or polygonOffset), barrel or turret clipping into the hull at extreme depression, track instances drifting off the wheels in reverse, and bloom/exposure washing out the hull under direct sun.

Questions to consider
- Which tank should be modelled — M1A2 Abrams, Leopard 2A7, T-90M, Type 99A, or a generic MBT? It changes silhouette, road-wheel count and the detail set (e.g. Abrams turbine vs T-90 diesel smoke).
- May three.js load from a public CDN (unpkg/jsdelivr), or must the page run fully offline? Offline would require vendoring/inlining three.js, which affects file size and the single-HTML promise.
- Target platform and control scheme: desktop keyboard+mouse only, or also touch/mobile, and do you want full driving physics or a stationary orbit-and-turret showcase?

- Tracks are the highest-ROI element: define one closed CatmullRomCurve3 around sprocket, idler, road wheels and return rollers, place link instances via InstancedMesh from curve.getPointAt/getTangentAt, and animate by advancing a scalar offset at (wheel angular velocity x radius) in both directions — so track speed matches ground speed instead of a fake texture scroll.
- For material realism use separate sets and generate their maps in-canvas: painted armour (roughness 0.6–0.75, metalness ~0.15) with procedural cast-steel mottling and edge chipping, bare steel tracks (metalness ~0.9, roughness ~0.45), rubber rims, and optical glass (roughness ~0.05, high envMapIntensity). RoomEnvironment + PMREM gives PBR reflections with no HDR file.
- Lighting/tone mapping decides whether it looks photographed: ACESFilmicToneMapping + SRGBColorSpace, one shadow-casting directional 'sun' with the shadow camera fitted tightly to the tank bounds, normalBias ~0.02 and bias ~-0.0005 to kill acne on flat armour plates, plus hemisphere fill and a subtle ground contact darkening.
- Post-processing is where 'showing off' is actually earned: EffectComposer chain of SSAO/GTAO -> bloom (threshold ~0.9 to avoid blowing out sunlit hull) -> SMAA, and a photo mode (P) with cinematic camera, BokehPass depth of field, vignette/grain and canvas screenshot download.
- Controls and feel: WASD torque-based drive with brake, independent 360-degree turret traverse and gun elevation clamped to roughly -9 to +20 degrees, mouse-look aiming, and firing that recoils the barrel ~0.3 m over ~60 ms with a damped hull rock, muzzle flash plus point-light flare, and a dust puff decal-free at the raycast impact point. Independent turret motion is what separates 'tank' from 'car with a gun'.
- Suspension: raycast each road wheel to a ground heightfield and offset wheels with damped springs, add slight hull pitch under acceleration/braking and a small speed-linked vibration for engine feel — cheap, and it removes the 'floating box' look while driving.
- Cameras and HUD: damped OrbitControls with polar limits so the ground is never seen from below, spring-follow chase camera, gunner's sight with an SVG NATO reticle and stepped 3x/10x zoom, commander panorama, and HUD readouts for speed, RPM/gear, turret azimuth, gun elevation, ammo state, FPS.
- Performance guardrails: InstancedMesh for tracks/bolts/ERA, shared geometries and materials, zero per-frame allocations (reuse scratch Vector3/Quaternion), pixelRatio capped at 2, and an auto-quality toggle that drops SSAO/DOF when frame time exceeds ~20 ms.
- Known failure modes to design against: z-fighting between layered armour plates (0.5–1 mm offsets or polygonOffset), barrel or turret clipping into the hull at extreme depression, track instances drifting off the wheels in reverse, and bloom/exposure washing out the hull under direct sun.

Questions to consider
- Which tank should be modelled — M1A2 Abrams, Leopard 2A7, T-90M, Type 99A, or a generic MBT? It changes silhouette, road-wheel count and the detail set (e.g. Abrams turbine vs T-90 diesel smoke).
- May three.js load from a public CDN (unpkg/jsdelivr), or must the page run fully offline? Offline would require vendoring/inlining three.js, which affects file size and the single-HTML promise.
- Target platform and control scheme: desktop keyboard+mouse only, or also touch/mobile, and do you want full driving physics or a stationary orbit-and-turret showcase?

Done — one file, [abrams-m1a2-showcase.html](abrams-m1a2-showcase.html) (128 KB, 2532 lines). Nothing else in the folder was opened; the only external reference is the pinned three.js r160 importmap.

## What it is
A procedurally generated **M1A2 SEP v3 Abrams** in real metres (3.92 × 9.95 m, 2.46 m to the turret roof, 94 track links per side) with a full real-time rig — nothing is loaded from disk: every texture is painted into a canvas at boot, and the sky/IBL is a procedural equirect run through PMREM.

| Mode | Controls |
|---|---|
| **ORBIT** | drag orbit, wheel zoom, right-drag pan |
| **DRIVE** | W/S throttle, A/D skid-steer (neutral steer at standstill), Space brake, B park |
| **AIM** | W/S/A/D auto-enters drive; mouse captures pointer for turret/gun |
| **FIRE** | LMB or Enter; 1/2/3 = M829A3 APFSDS / M830A1 HEAT-MP / M1028 canister; R = laser rangefinder; V or wheel = 3×/10× optic |
| **TAB** cycles orbit → drive → gunner → photo; P = photo mode (DOF, drag frame, S saves a 2× PNG) |

Details that survive a close orbit: hinged skirt panels with ERA tiles, mesh bustle rack with stowage, 2×6 smoke banks, segmented thermal sleeve + bore evacuator + barrel name decal, M2 and M240 with ammo belts, CITV/GPS sight glass, weld beads and bolt rows (instanced), tow bars, antennas that sway, TUSK ERA, and star/unit markings. Driving leaves real track prints and dust; firing recoils 0.16 m with a hull rock, muzzle flash with a point light, and a shell that flies, impacts and scorches the ground. Audio (turbine whine, track clatter, cannon boom delayed by distance) is synthesised with WebAudio — off by default.

## Verification — and its limit
No browser could be launched here (headless Edge is blocked by the sandbox), so **not one pixel has been rendered by me.** What I *could* do is extract the module and run the real code under Node against three r160, which found and fixed several genuine defects:

- **bbox 3.92 × 9.95 m**, turret roof 2.460 m, muzzle 1.920 m past the nose, gun axis 2.015 m — no toy-scale drift
- 251 meshes, 1812 instances, ~93k tris, 0 NaN; terrain normals all up; **two inversions caught and fixed** (a barrel lathe whose profile ran the wrong way, and terrain triangles wound so every normal pointed down)
- tracks: closed curve, link gap 0.168 m = pitch, identical y-range forward *and* reverse, link travels aft when driving forward, wheels roll the right way
- driving 0→55.8 km/h, brake to 0, suspension travel sane, contact shadow conforms to the terrain to 0.0000 m
- **barrel never enters the deck**: worst clearance 0.385 m across a full 360° yaw sweep, with a realistic deck-clearance inhibit clamping depression to −3.2° when traversed aft

An independent appearance review then produced changes I applied and re-verified: the composer now owns pass sizing (my resize was silently halving bloom/AO on HiDPI), DOF aperture was saturating 0.4 m from focus, bloom threshold moved to 1.05 in linear HDR, shadow frustum tightened with texel snapping, and the materials de-chromed (paint is now a dielectric, glass non-metallic). It also caught that my boot camera sat behind the vehicle — the hero frame is now a lit three-quarter front-right with the gun crossing the frame.

So: geometry, rigging, physics and logic are measured and clean (`ERRORS=0`). The addon chain, boot and first frame are **unverified** — an independent review returned "unverified" for exactly that reason, and I'm not going to claim otherwise. I've wrapped those paths so a failure degrades (direct render, environment fallback, error text in the loading overlay) rather than a black screen. Open it and if anything looks off, paste the console output or a screenshot and I'll fix it.
